title: Go‑Live Stakeholder Governance and Communications Playbook
author: Asha Kumar
body:
Overview:

This playbook defines the governance, stakeholder communications, and operational handoffs required for enterprise customer go‑lives at Redwood Inference. It is intended for Customer Success (CS), Solutions Engineering (SE), Product, Support (SRE/TS), and the customer’s technical and business stakeholders. The goal is to ensure predictable launches with clear responsibilities, timely escalation, and structured post‑go‑live monitoring.

Scope:

- Applies to all enterprise go‑lives that meet one or more criteria: Dedicated or Private deployment, monthly committed spend >= $50k, regulated data requirements, or multi‑region routing.
- Covers pre‑go‑live governance checkpoints, the 72‑hour go‑live window, and the first 30 days of post‑go‑live operations.

Key Principles:

1. Single source‑of‑truth: the CS go‑live checklist (linked in related_pages) is the canonical status tracker.
2. Clear RACI: every task has an owner and an escalation contact.
3. Time‑boxed decisioning: critical rollback or mitigation decisions must be made within defined SLAs.
4. Transparent customer communications: status updates use agreed templates and cadence.

Stakeholder RACI (high level):

| Role | Responsible | Accountable | Consulted | Informed |
|------|-------------|-------------|-----------|---------|
| Customer Success (CS) | Onboarding plan, customer comms | CS Director | SE, Support | Customer execs, Product |
| Solutions Engineering (SE) | Integration, pre‑prod validation | SE Lead | CS, Support | Customer engineering |
| Support / SRE | Runbooks, incident triage | Support Manager | SE, CS, Infra | Customer ops |
| Product | Feature rollouts, gating | Product Manager | SE, CS | Exec stakeholders |
| Customer Engineering | Application integration | Customer Eng Lead | CS, SE | Customer execs |

Pre‑Go‑Live checkpoints (must be complete to schedule go‑live):

- Security and compliance gate: signed checklist covering encryption, KMS integration, data residency (owner: Security/CS).
- Traffic modelling completed with expected peak RPS and token volumes (owner: SE).
- Capacity reservation for Dedicated/private and autoscale policies validated (owner: Infra/SRE).
- Monitoring and alerting: dashboards created, synthetic probes configured, runbooks attached (owner: Support).
- Business stakeholders sign go‑live readiness form (owner: CS).

Go‑Live Window (72 hours) — Roles & Cadence:

1. Communications cadence:
   - T‑24h: Readiness confirmation email to all stakeholders (CS).
   - T0: Go‑live kickoff Slack channel opened, 15‑minute sync with CS, SE, Support, customer lead.
   - T+4h: First status update to customer (successful/partial/failure + actions).
   - T+24h: Formal health report (latency, error rate, cost burn vs forecast).
   - T+72h: 72‑hour summary and recommendation (continue, throttle, rollback).

2. On‑call coverage:
   - Support single point of contact (SPOC) must be on call for the 72h window and 7 days after for critical customers.
   - Escalation contact list (primary, secondary, tertiary) must be published in the kickoff Slack channel and in the CS checklist.

Operational thresholds and automatic actions (examples):

- Production error rate > 3% for 5 minutes: create SE+Support bridge immediately.
- 99th percentile latency > 2x expected SLA for 10 minutes: trigger capacity increase and notify CS.
- Unexpected cost burn > 150% of forecast for 1 hour: autoscale down to safe minimum and notify finance & CS.
- Persistent KV cache misses causing >20% throughput drop: enable temporary traffic routing to fallback model variant.

Escalation Path and SLAs:

1. Triage: 15 minutes to assign incident if alert fires during go‑live.
2. Severity 1 (production outage or P99 latency > 5x): 15 minute response, 60 minute mitigation plan.
3. Severity 2 (partial degradation): 30 minute response, 3 hour mitigation plan.
4. Severity 3 (minor issues/no customer impact): respond within 4 hours.

Escalation contacts (example):

- Primary Support SPOC: support-oncall@redwood.ai (Pager: +1 555 0101)
- SE Lead: se-leads@redwood.ai (Slack: #se‑oncall)
- CS Director: cs-director@redwood.ai

Communication templates (use verbatim or customer‑branded variants) — Email: T‑24h Readiness

Subject: [Redwood] Go‑Live readiness confirmation for <Customer Name> — <YYYY‑MM‑DD>

Hello <Customer Stakeholder>,

We are confirming the go‑live window for <Customer Name> on <YYYY‑MM‑DD> (T0). Below is the plan and contacts: 

- Kickoff: <HH:MM> (UTC) — Slack: #<customer‑go‑live‑channel>
- Support SPOC: <Name> (<phone>)
- SE Lead: <Name>
- Escalation policy: Severity criteria and SLAs attached.

Please reply to confirm or flag any outstanding issues.

Best,
<CS Owner>

Slack status message (short):

GO‑LIVE: <Customer> • T0 <HH:MM UTC> • Support SPOC: <Name> • Runbook: <link>

Go‑Live Checklist (condensed table view):

| Item | Owner | Status | Notes |
|------|-------|--------|-------|
| Security gate signed | Security/CS | complete | KMS validated |
| Capacity reserved | Infra/SRE | complete | 4 GPU units, autoscale |
| Integration tests green | SE | complete | sample traffic 5k RPS |
| Monitoring dashboards | Support | complete | Alerts: 3 configured |
| Customer exec signoff | CS | complete | Email 2025‑10‑30 |

Rollback criteria and process:

- Rollback should be considered if any of the following persist for >30 minutes despite mitigation attempts:
  1. Service outage impacting >10% of customer traffic.
  2. Error rate >5% with customer‑visible failures.
  3. Cost burn escalating >200% of committed forecast and billing risk.

Rollback steps (owner: SE + Support):

1. Convene immediate bridge and notify CS and customer execs.
2. Execute rollback plan to previous model version/traffic routing (Runbook: rollback‑model‑vN).
3. Validate functional baseline with synthetic probes for 15 minutes.
4. Communicate rollback outcome and next steps to customer and internal execs.

Post‑Go‑Live: 30‑day health plan and QBR inputs:

- Daily health digest for first 7 days (CS/Support): latency distribution, error rate, cost vs forecast, key customer incidents.
- Weekly check‑in calls for first 4 weeks: CS + Customer Eng + SE to review operational tuning and prompt set regressions.
- QBR inputs (collected at day 30): adoption metrics, cost per 1k tokens, top 5 regressions detected, feature requests.

Minimum monitoring dashboard items (copyable list):

- Token throughput (tokens/sec) by route
- 50/95/99 latency percentiles by model
- Error rate (4xx/5xx) by service and model
- Cache hit ratio (KV cache)
- Cost per 1M tokens rolling 24h
- Synthetic end‑to‑end success rate (every 5m)

Appendix A — Example CLI for synthetic probe (copy into SE runbook):

#!/bin/bash
# run synthetic prompt against production route and record latency
PROMPT='Summarize these 3 bullets.'
ROUTE='https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate?route=customer‑<id>'
START=$(date +%s%3N)
RESPONSE=$(curl -s -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"input":"'$PROMPT'","max_tokens":64}' "$ROUTE")
END=$(date +%s%3N)
LATENCY=$((END-START))
echo "latency_ms=$LATENCY response_len=$(echo $RESPONSE | wc -c)"

Ownership and maintenance:

- Document owner: Asha Kumar (Customer Success) — responsible for updates and running the go‑live postmortem.
- Review cadence: Biannual or after any major incident that occurs within 30 days of a go‑live.

Change log: 

- 2025‑11‑02: Created by A. Kumar (initial template).
- 2026‑01‑18: Clarified escalation SLAs and added automatic cost mitigation triggers (reviewer: J. Li).
- 2026‑02‑12: Added 72‑hour detailed cadence and sample CLI probe (reviewer: M. Petrova).

Notes and best practices (quick tips):

- Always confirm the customer inbox and Slack channel recipients at T‑24h to avoid missed notifications.
- Run a dry‑run with synthetic traffic 48–72h before the window to catch infra bottlenecks.
- Keep customer‑facing updates concise: status, action, ETA.
- Empirically record the actions taken during go‑live in the checklist so postmortems have accurate timelines.
